title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: A program always does the same three things in the same order: it runs search_manuals, passes the result to the model to write an answer, and stops. Answer in one word: what owns the control flow here, the code or the model?
Which statement best tells a workflow apart from an agent?

options.text: A workflow uses no language model, while an agent always calls one
An agent calls tools, while a workflow never calls any tool at all
A workflow runs fewer steps, while an agent always runs more steps
In a workflow, code fixes the steps; in an agent, the model chooses them

items.stem: Your sponsor's budget is small. Which part of the makerspace assistant is the best candidate for a fixed workflow instead of an agent?

options.text: Answering a question that may need several manuals, in an order unknown beforehand
Booking a slot: check the calendar, write the booking, send the confirmation email
Working out why a machine's output looks wrong from a student's description of it
Suggesting which machine suits a student's unusual project idea, with trade-offs

items.stem: Your sponsor's budget allows 1,200 model calls per month. A fixed workflow for booking requests always makes exactly 3 model calls per request. At most how many booking requests can it serve in a month?

A program makes one model call that reads a student's message and returns a single label: "manual question", "booking" or "other". The code then runs the fixed path written for that label. Who owns the control flow?

options.text: The model, because its decision changes which steps happen next
The model, because it is the only part that reads the message
The code, because it defines every path and the model only picks one
Neither, because the routing is shared equally by code and model

items.stem: Agents cost more model calls than fixed workflows. Which feature of a task best justifies paying that cost?

options.text: The steps needed depend on what earlier results turn up, so they cannot be listed in advance
The task is very common, so many students will ask for it every single day
The task has several steps, so the model has to be called once for each of them
The task must be answered correctly, so extra model calls are needed to check it
